brief:
We Are Not Numbers published a speculative piece envisioning a FIFA World Cup held in Palestine, depicting a stadium constructed amid conflict rubble and children in traditional embroidered clothing carrying olive branches at the opening ceremony.

The essay frames the hypothetical tournament as symbolic reconstruction, contrasting the image of a new sporting venue rising from devastated terrain with the physical destruction that characterizes the region's landscape. It employs the World Cup scenario to explore themes of cultural pride and national identity through Palestinian traditions and youth participation in the ceremony.

The piece appears designed to prompt readers to imagine conditions under which such an international event could take place in the territory, using sports infrastructure and ceremonial pageantry as vehicles for examining Palestinian self-determination and cultural expression.
dek: Imagine a new stadium rising from the rubble, and children dressed in traditional embroidered garments walking onto the field carrying olive branches!.
title: Essay imagines World Cup hosted in Palestinian territories
